answer.reason: The verses tell of Absalom's killing of Amnon, his revolt against David, and his death in the oak, which go beyond the summary.

clauses.english: had his servants kill his brother Amnon at the sheepshearing, then fled to Geshur
clauses.quote: Smite Amnon; then kill him, fear not

clauses.english: stole the hearts of the men of Israel and rose in revolt, so that David fled from Jerusalem
clauses.quote: so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel

clauses.english: was caught by his head in an oak and was thrust through the heart
clauses.quote: thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak

doubts: The first clause joins the killing of Amnon with the flight to Geshur; the flight may be better dropped as a separate event.
1KI 1:6 and 1KI 2:28 mention Absalom only to place others in relation to him, so they are left out.
2SA 14:21-33 (his return to Jerusalem and meeting with the king) was left out as a lesser event.
